1.title: Task 1: Component Identification
1.description: One of the first tasks that you must perform is to identify and list all components associated with Operational Technology (OT).
1.instructions:
Review the provided scenario and answer each question thoroughly.

  1. Component Identification

    Carefully examine all three exhibits (Network Topology, Ladder Logic, and HMI Display). Identify distinct hardware and software components crucial to the operation and security of this system. Examples include, but are not limited to: PLCs, HMIs, Historians, Firewalls, Sensors, etc.

  2. Function Description

    For each of the components you identify, provide a concise but accurate description of its primary function within the industrial environment and, specifically, as it relates to the operation of the system.

  3. Purdue Model Layer Placement

    Using the Purdue Model, determine the appropriate layer for each identified component. Justify your placement based on the component's function and its relationship to other systems.

Deliverable Format

Organize your findings into a clear and well-structured table using the following columns:

  • Component Name/Type: The specific name of the hardware or software component (e.g., Siemens S7-1500, OPC Server, Ethernet/IP Switch).
  • Exhibit Source: Indicate which exhibit(s) the component was identified in (e.g., Network Topology, Ladder Logic, HMI Display).
  • Primary Function: A 1-2 sentence description of what the component does.
  • Purdue Model Layer: The corresponding level number (0-5) and name (e.g., Level 3: Manufacturing Operations System).
  • Justification: A brief explanation of why this layer is the correct placement for the component.

Example Component Identification Table

2.title: Task 2: Threat Intelligence
2.description: Develop PLC programs to meet the scenario requirements.
2.instructions:
Assume the industrial facility operates in the Food and Beverage Sector (Cookie Factory) and utilizes the components identified in Task 1. You must now focus on preventing future security incidents by considering known threats to this sector, where production integrity and hygiene are paramount.

  1. Industry-Specific Attack Vector Identification

    Identify three (3) distinct, high-probability attack vectors that a threat actor (internal or external) could use to compromise the cookie factory. Focus on vectors that specifically target the vulnerabilities common in the F&B sector (e.g., supply chain disruption, recipe modification, hygiene control systems) or the types of devices (e.g., PLCs, batch control systems, inventory systems) identified in Task 1. Describe the potential path an attacker would take for each vector.

  2. Current and Historical Threat Analysis

    Based on documented incidents or known vulnerabilities (e.g., targeting of proprietary recipe databases, contamination scares, exploitation of temperature/batch controllers), select a specific, historical, or active threat relevant to the F&B or general ICS environment.

    • Describe the Threat: Briefly explain what this specific threat targets and its typical impact on a food manufacturing process (e.g., loss of batch quality, product recall, physical damage).
    • Affected Component: Identify one component from Task 1 that this threat is most likely to affect (e.g., the batch controller, the Historian, a conveyor PLC).

  3. Security Control Selection and Mapping

    For each of the three (3) attack vectors identified in Step 1, propose a specific and layered preventive security control (e.g., technical solution, policy, or procedural measure). Map the selected control to the Mitre ATT&CK ICS framework or relevant cybersecurity standards for comprehensive coverage.

Deliverable Format

Organize your findings into a concise, actionable security brief using the following table format:

Paragraphs explaining the steps you took to analyze and mitigate the threats followed by a table summarizing your findings.

Attack Vector IdentifiedPotential Attacker PathRecommended Security ControlPurdue Model Layer for Implementation
Integrity Compromise via Recipe DatabaseAttacker compromises the Level 4 MES/Recipe server via a phishing email, then modifies batch parameters (e.g., ingredient ratios, oven temperature setpoints) before they are sent to the Level 2 batch controller.Strict access control and integrity monitoring (e.g., file hashing, change control) on all master recipe and batch files stored on Level 4/3 servers.This maps to Mitre ATT&CK ICS framework technique ID T0834 (Modify Control Logic)

3.title: Task 3: Cyber-Informed Engineering
3.description: Identify controls to mitigate destruction of equipment and hazards to personnel.
3.instructions:
Cyber-Informed Engineering (CIE) integrates cybersecurity considerations into the engineering design and operational processes of industrial systems. In this task, you will apply CIE principles to enhance the security posture of the cookie factory's OT system. This Task is going to require you to research Engineering controls like physical safeguards, fail-safe mechanisms, and intrusion detection systems.

Identify and describe five (5) engineering controls or design modifications that could be implemented to mitigate the risk of equipment destruction or hazards to personnel resulting from cyber-attacks. Consider both physical and cyber controls that align with industry best practices.

Deliverable Format:

This section should be written in paragraph format. Organize your thoughts clearly and provide detailed explanations for each proposed control or modification.

Important: I understand that you are not experienced Engineers. I do not expect you to know the specific engineering controls (i.e. light curtain, lock out/tag out, etc.). Do your best to research and propose reasonable controls. The important part here is that you identify the potential problems and propose thoughtful mitigations.

4.title: Task 4: Supply Chain Security
4.description: Identify and assess risks associated with the supply chain.
4.instructions: Supply chain security is a critical aspect of OT cybersecurity, as vulnerabilities in the supply chain can lead to significant risks for industrial systems. In this task, you are working with your procurement department to write a contract to implement the engineering controls you identified in Task 3. You are required to give detailed descriptions of the items to purchase, expected costs of the items, and the required service level agreement you need from the vendor.
